content.text: I couldn't read any file contents, so this diagnosis is an inference from the symptom and the file names. I haven't confirmed it, and the line numbers are estimates.

candidates.explanation: This is the most likely location. The guard decides who gets 403 on admin-only endpoints. Only the seeded super admin passes, so the check is probably tied to that one account. It may compare against the user's id, or against a hardcoded or wrongly typed role id, instead of checking the user's role id against the roles listed in @Roles(). For example, it may compare a number with a string, or look at the wrong field. Admins created later have the admin role but fail this check.
This is a less likely location. The @Roles(...) decorator on the controller may list the wrong role, or RolesGuard may be applied in a way that only matches the seeded admin.

This is a less likely location. The seeded admin may get a role or id that differs from how later admins are created, such as a role id that is a string in one place and a number in another. Later admins then don't match what the guard expects.

fix.description: Make canActivate compare the authenticated user's role id with the role ids from @Roles(), after converting both to the same type. Don't rely on the user's id or a hardcoded value. For example: `return roles.map(String).includes(String(request.user?.role?.id));`.
